name: Cold Reach
tagline: Outreach that gets replies, not unsubscribes
about: Cold Reach writes multi-touch outreach sequences across email, LinkedIn and phone, personalises each touch from what you actually know about the prospect, and tells you what to say when they reply.
persona: You are a top-performing SDR coach: concise, specific, allergic to buzzwords and fake personalisation; every message leads with the prospect's problem, not the product.

onboarding.title: Book more first meetings
onboarding.subtitle: Tell us what you sell and who buys it; every message will be built around that.

profile.label: What you sell
profile.placeholder: expense management software for mid-size finance teams

profile.label: Who buys it
profile.placeholder: CFOs and controllers at 200–2,000 employee companies

tools.title: Build a sequence
tools.subtitle: Email + LinkedIn + call touches

inputs.label: Prospect persona
inputs.placeholder: VP Finance at a Series C fintech

tools.prompt: Write a {length}-touch cold outreach sequence for {persona} using {channels}, selling the profile's product in the profile's tone. Sections: a table (Day | Channel | Goal | Hook) laying out the cadence, then one quote section per touch with the full copy (subject line under 5 words for emails, under 300 characters for LinkedIn notes, a 20-second opener for calls), and a callout naming the single most common mistake to avoid with this persona.

tools.title: Personalise a touch
tools.subtitle: Paste their LinkedIn bio or post

inputs.label: Profile / bio / recent post
inputs.placeholder: Head of RevOps at Acme. Posted last week about forecasting pain…

tools.prompt: From this prospect info: {bio} — write a {touch} that references two specific, non-creepy details and ties them to the profile's product. Sections: bullets listing the details you chose and why, a quote with the final message (under 90 words for email, under 300 characters for a connect note, under 30 seconds spoken for voicemail), and kv (Hook used | Ask | Best send time).

tools.title: Cold subject lines
tools.subtitle: 10 lines for a cold email, ranked

inputs.label: Email body
inputs.placeholder: paste the email you plan to send

tools.prompt: For this cold email to a prospect who has never heard of us: {email} — generate 10 subject lines in the {style} style as a table (Subject | Angle | Open tier: High/Med/Low | Spam-word risk). Then bullets with the 3 preview-text lines that pair best with the top subject, and a callout on words and formatting that trigger spam filters.

tools.title: They replied — now what?
tools.subtitle: Turn any reply into a next step

inputs.label: Their reply
inputs.placeholder: Thanks but we're all set with our current vendor.

tools.prompt: The prospect replied: {reply_text}. Context, if any: {context}. Classify the reply in kv (Type | Real meaning | Win probability), then write 2 response options as quote sections (one short and low-pressure, one that reframes with a question), and steps for what to do if they go silent again.

tools.title: Break-up email
tools.subtitle: The last touch that gets replies

inputs.label: What you've sent so far
inputs.placeholder: 4 emails about invoice automation over 3 weeks, no reply

tools.prompt: Write a break-up email closing this sequence: {thread}. Sections: a quote with the email (under 60 words, no guilt-tripping, one clear door left open), bullets with 3 alternative closing lines for different personas, and a callout on when to actually re-engage (timing and trigger events).

disclaimer: Cold outreach is regulated: check consent, opt-out and B2B rules that apply where your prospects live (CAN-SPAM, GDPR, PECR, CASL) before sending, and honour every unsubscribe.
